title: EPR as a probe for the mechanisms of chirality-induced spin selectivity in photoinduced charge transfer
authors: Arianna Cantarella, D. K. Andrea Phan Huu, Paolo Santini, Michael R. Wasielewski, Alessandro Chiesa, Stefano Carretta
abstract: Several models for chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) in charge transfer have been proposed, but rarely compared directly with experiments. This step is essential for their validation and future progress of the field. Here we investigate a broad class of radical pair states associated with different microscopic models by computing the related electron-paramagnetic resonance spectra. This allows us to evidence peculiar signatures of different radical pair states, to study their experimental accessibility and identify conditions to verify proposed microscopic models.
summary: This paper investigates Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) in charge transfer processes by simulating Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectra. The authors use the radical-pair Hamiltonian to predict how molecular chirality influences the spin state of separated charges. By comparing simulated spectra under various field orientations, they provide a powerful, measurable diagnostic tool to validate theoretical models of CISS.
main_problem: The primary goal is to validate theoretical models for Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) in photoinduced charge transfer (PCT) by comparing predicted Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) spectra with experimental observables.
main_result: The study demonstrates that the TREPR spectrum is a sensitive diagnostic tool, showing distinct spectral signatures when CISS effects are present, particularly when the magnetic field is oriented perpendicular to the dipolar axis in aligned samples.
method: The authors compute spin dynamics using the radical-pair Hamiltonian and calculate the resulting Triplet Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (TREPR) spectra via linear response theory.
model_or_system: The system involves radical pairs formed during charge transfer in chiral molecules, governed by a Hamiltonian incorporating electron-electron interactions and spin-orbit coupling (SOC). The analysis extends beyond simple collinear assumptions to model general spin polarization orientations.
key_observables: The primary diagnostic tool is the TREPR spectrum; CISS efficiency ($\eta$) is related to the triplet population $p = (1 - \cos \chi)$.
important_parameters: The magnetic field ($\mathbf{B}_0$) orientation relative to the dipolar axis, the degree of spin polarization ($\chi$), and the molecular geometry parameters.
main_assumptions: Initial models often assume the CISS axis is collinear with the dipolar axis, and some analyses assume the initial state is a pure spin state, neglecting post-projection coherences.
figures_summary: Figures simulate powder and oriented-sample TREPR spectra showing spectral changes for varying CISS contributions (0%, 50%, 100%) and field/polarization orientations relative to the dipolar axis.
paper_structure: The work progresses by first establishing the general Hamiltonian and the TREPR calculation method, then moving to simulations that explore non-collinear polarization states using oriented samples (LC) to reveal key spectral signatures.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges molecular chirality, spin physics, and measurable spectroscopic techniques (EPR), which is highly relevant to AMO physics, particularly in the study of open quantum systems and spin dynamics in molecular complexes.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Simulated powder TREPR spectra for an initial triplet polarization along different molecular-frame directions for a prototypical molecule in Q-band. The directions are parametrized by the polar angle α from the CT axis (β = 0 throughout). Panel (a): polarization direction parallel to the CT axis (α = 0◦); panel (d): polarization direction orthogonal to the CT axis (α = 90◦); panels (b,c) show intermediate orientations. Each panel reports spectra for CISS contributions of 0%, 50%, and 100%.

FIG. 2. Simulated oriented-sample TREPR spectra for the four combinations of polarization orientation relative to the dipolar axis, for a prototypical molecule, in Q-band. Rows: orientation of the polarization vector relative to the molecular dipolar axis (parallel, top; perpendicular, bottom). Columns: orientation of the external magnetic field B0 relative to the dipolar axis (B0 ∥, left; B0 ⊥, right). In each panel, spectra are shown for CISS contributions of 0%, 50%, and 100%.
